# Soundings

> Soundings helps organisations improve workplace culture through workshops, coaching, programmes, and practical resources. Based in the UK, working with charities, NHS/public sector organisations, and scaling businesses.

Soundings is led by Sam Kammerling, an organisational development practitioner with a background spanning the NHS, social research, and mental health work. The practice is grounded in evidence, honest about uncertainty, and focused on change that lasts beyond the engagement.

The name "Soundings" refers to the nautical practice of taking soundings — finding out the true depth of what lies beneath before acting.

## Services

- **Workshops** — facilitated sessions that name difficult issues, build shared language, and surface practical tools teams can use immediately
- **Coaching** — individual and leadership coaching focused on honesty, clarity, and starting from what matters most
- **Programmes** — multi-month culture and management development engagements for organisations that want change to last
- **Practical Resources** — videos, frameworks, and conversation tools made for specific organisational contexts

## Who we work with

Charities, NHS trusts, public sector bodies, and scaling SMEs — organisations where culture matters but genuine culture change is hard. Audiences include senior leaders, management teams, HR leads, and L&D professionals.

## Founder

**Sam Kammerling** — organisational development practitioner, facilitator, and coach. Background in NHS workforce development, social research, and mental health sector work. Sam brings warmth, directness, and a grounding in what the research actually says about how organisations change.

## Selected writing

- [Nothing is Transformative](https://thesoundings.co.uk/nothing-is-transformative.html): Why the consulting industry's obsession with transformation is mostly self-serving, and what genuinely useful change actually looks like
- [A Simple Tool for Making Conflict a Bit Less Rubbish](https://thesoundings.co.uk/conflict-tool.html): On the instinct to win or self-punish when disagreements arise, and one reframe that changes everything
- [Fear and Loathing in Las Workplace](https://thesoundings.co.uk/fear-and-loathing.html): Why fear is an accepted norm in most workplaces, how it produces inhuman behaviour, and three ways to start pushing back
